question: S-E6 measured two similarity defects and proposed fixes. Do the fixes work?
decision_it_changes: Whether IDF weighting and adaptive view combination ship, and whether Dataset B's 6-cluster result is defensible. Recorded as the ADR-021 addendum.
dataset: dataset_a (frozen S-E4 segmentation) for tasks 1-3; dataset_b for task 4
segmentation: FROZEN — 1,717 segments, boundary F1 0.6904 @ tau=2 s, count ratio 0.98. Asserted identical on every arm in metrics.json.contract_boundary_f1.

tasks.1: IDF-weight every set-based similarity (surfaces, routes, origins, bigrams, element ids, field keys). Acceptance test: case study 3's 99%.
tasks.2: adaptive / noisy-OR view combination. Acceptance test: case studies 1 and 2's 13.3%.
tasks.3: scaffolding contamination — counted and reported, NEVER removed from the pipeline.
tasks.4: Dataset B internal consistency; regenerate segments.jsonl.

ablation_design: The shipped S-E6 configuration (where_heavy, k_nn=20) is held fixed; only IDF on/off and the combination mode vary, so each delta is attributable to one factor.
population: scoreable canonical, tiers clean+repaired, 63 sessions; 1,332 of 1,752 reference fragments matched at IoU 0.5 (match_rate 0.760), 15 reference codes
reuse: procmine/evaluate.py evaluate_all -> identity_scores / matched_identity / interruption_recall. No metric reimplemented.
non_goals: no metric learning from LLM pseudo-labels
not_done: Task 5 (pretrained multilingual embedding probe) was optional on 60 minutes remaining. It was not reached and no dependency was added.
reporting_rules: ARI never without match_rate, homogeneity and completeness
a case-study rate is only comparable within one arm
